The attract demo starts a dive at G.t=180 (line 311), so the title screen crashes and freezes at 3.0 s (animates_idle=false). Also destroyEnemy is called at line 269 but never defined.

bugs.text: spawnStage builds the 40-enemy layout but never assigns it to G.enemies (only boot() at line 402 does), so no enemy ever appears in a started game; stages 1 and 2 'complete' in 75 frames each with nothing on screen.
Space never fires: the keydown handler does not call playerFire; its only caller is the attract demo. The player cannot shoot at all.

startDive/endBeam never set e.ctrl, which updateDive passes to bez: every dive throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading x)' each frame, aborting update() before render(). This freezes the attract screen 3 s after load (192 page errors, animates_idle=false) and would freeze play on the first dive.

Challenge stage soft-lock: wave 1 spawns, the 8 Zako loop once (t clamped to 1) and park off-screen at x=-20/-56 forever; they never die or leave, so advanceChallenge never runs again and the game is stuck in stage 3 within about 5 s of pressing Enter (all five play screenshots are empty).
destroyEnemy is called when an enemy rams the player but is never defined: a ram throws ReferenceError.
No respawn: after 'READY' expires the dead player is never revived (line 211 is p.x=p.x), the ship vanishes and play continues with an invisible, unkillable player with lives left.
Boss hits counter is never initialised: e.hits++ gives NaN, so a Boss can never be destroyed and never changes colour.
Stage badge loop breaks before drawing for any stage under 50; exactly one '1' flag is shown for stages 1-49.
Formation sway amplitude is 0.7*slot.x (up to 103 px): the formation squeezes toward x=0 and swings off the right edge instead of swaying uniformly; no breathing phase.
No 'STAGE N' text is ever shown, and after GAME OVER the game stays in the gameOver state with the HUD; it never returns to the title screen.
High score is drawn twice (centred and right-aligned), so three score numbers appear on the HUD.
Canvas is a fixed 224x288 pixels with no scaling to the window; the playfield is tiny on any normal display.
Captive docking (sets G.dual) and starfield movement happen inside render(), tying game state and star speed to the refresh rate.
No hit-results screen (shots fired / hits / ratio) at game over although the counters are kept.
Challenge wave bonus compares the cumulative hit count to 8, so after one full wave every later wave gets the 1,000 bonus regardless of hits.
Shooting a Boss in formation frees and docks the captive instead of destroying it; a dual-fighter hit kills the whole player (line 186) rather than one half.
GOEI sprite row 4 is 6 characters wide instead of 7, misaligning the butterfly's lower body.

summary: The file is organised the way the spec asks (a state object, a fixed-step update, a render pass, pixel sprites, synthesized Web Audio) and on paper touches almost every feature: entry arcs, dives, re-entry, tractor beam, capture, rescue, dual fighter, challenge waves, extra ships, explosions, seven sounds. In practice almost none of it runs. spawnStage forgets to store the enemies it builds, so a started game has no enemies; the input handler never calls playerFire, so the player can never shoot; every dive dereferences an unset control point and throws, which freezes the attract screen three seconds after load; a rammed enemy calls a function that does not exist; the Boss hit counter is NaN so a Boss can never die; the challenge stage parks its first wave off-screen and never ends, soft-locking the game by stage 3; and a dead player is never respawned. The code reads like a sketch that was never run once: dense one-line functions, state changes inside render, a dangling comment about a simpler approach, hitboxes double the sprite size, and a stage-badge loop that breaks before drawing. What the title screen shows for its first three seconds, a 40-enemy formation flying in behind a GALAGA logo and score table, is the only moment it resembles Galaga.
